boundary_decision.rationale: The root is a persistent versioned rule expression with its own identity, authority, applicability and evaluation contract. Evaluations, decisions and enforcement occur around it but do not turn the rule itself into an event.

decisions.rationale: The model owns one reusable rule and its immutable revisions rather than requirement-record authorship, validation execution or accountable enforcement.
A requirement may source or own the rule, but canonical inheritance requires joint boundary review because rules also originate in policies, standards and other authorities.
Requirement, constraint, invariant, business rule, validation shape, policy rule and legal norm use distinct modality and authority semantics.
Operands, operators, datatypes, units, logic, input snapshot, engine and profile must be source-qualified and versioned.
Syntax validity, satisfaction, verification, validation, conformance, compliance, safety, legal effect and accountable decision are separate claims.
Departures and precedence resolutions require explicit scope, authority, rationale, conditions, effective time and expiry while source rules remain visible.
OCL, DMN, SHACL, OWL, SPARQL, ODRL, LegalRuleML, XACML, JSON Schema, Schematron, OSCAL, OpenAPI and Rego views do not replace canonical rule identity.
Agents may append low-risk formalizations and evaluations but not approve, waive, enforce, disclose protected data or destroy records without authority.

publication_holds: Absence-of-external-review hold: one Claude Sonnet attempt timed out and one Grok attempt failed before producing an admissible result; no external result was admitted.
Relation hold: WM-REC-006 remains a reference rather than an approved parent until joint boundary review.
Boundary hold: requirements, policies, standards, controls, systems, objects, tests, evidence, decisions, exceptions and enforcement actions remain external masters.
Profile hold: engineering, business, validation, legal, access-control, safety and compliance rules require domain-specific semantics.
Evaluation hold: syntax validity, rule satisfaction, verification, validation, conformance, compliance, safety and legal effect remain distinct.
Exception hold: waivers, deviations, conflicts and precedence require accountable authority, bounded scope, rationale and time.
Engine hold: executable evaluation requires pinned rule revision, input snapshot, engine, built-ins, profile, clock and outcome vocabulary.
Interoperability hold: every standards projection requires exact release pins, conformance tests and semantic-loss declarations.
Completeness hold: the 24-source draft is broad but does not claim universal domain, legal, logical, safety or operational coverage.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.
